proposals.evidence: Turner gives the full bhrātṛ brother family, including Lahnda bhirā, Punjabi bhā/bhāī, Pahari bhai/bhau, eastern bhāi and Kohistani žā/ẓā. These simple survey responses match the regional brother stems; bhaiyā and related affectionate/inflected endings are kept with the lexical base. The older/younger distinction belongs to the elicitation context, and responses containing only small/young adjectives or mixed alternatives are excluded.

proposals.evidence: Turner gives bhaginī sister through both peripheral bhaïṇī and central bahiṇī, with Punjabi bhaiṇ, Nepali baini, Oriya bhaüṇī and Kohistani bhẽ/bhī̃/bihā̃. The selected complete survey sister forms preserve these regional developments and ordinary affectionate endings. Bare bāī/bhayā forms are excluded where woman/sister or brother homonymy needs separate evidence.

proposals.evidence: Turner explicitly groups western Pahari dēddī/daiddī, Kumaoni didī/dī and Nepali/Bengali/Oriya didi elder sister under *diddā. These survey didi/di variants match the nursery kinship family, with retroflex spellings retained as a qualification; this does not claim a uniquely inherited rather than diffusional history for the nursery term.
